title: the DSG cave-ins part II - the chain reactions and the effects

banner.title: The DSG CAVE-INS PART II, R512: the printed pp. 39-40 (pdf 40-41) - the chain reactions (even a small cave-in weakening supporting structures, the nearby ceilings and walls checked, the per-section d100 vs Table 18, the equal-or-less collapse at about the same area, the within-10% significant weakening, the forced adjacent checks with the tertiary chance half rounded up and each subsequent roll halved, the decayed exception keeping the original chance, the 9th-level druid transmute rock to mud example with the 31-vs-48 collapse, the 42-vs-24 hold, the side rolls 12/65/97/33, the secondary 1/2 and tertiary 1/4) and the effects (the falling distance and rough landing on top, the bridge along its unsupported length, the tunnel ceiling never wider than the tunnel, the random 20x20 roughly square base area, the chain checks per adjacent square radically increasing the size, the three-foot layer assumption with the two-foot example, the 4d8 per 10 feet of thickness with the save vs petrification for half, the 30-foot 12d8 example reduced to 6d8, the mud and silt at half with the save halving again, and the water at half with a save for 1/4, the first 10-foot thickness only, no weight damage, the drowning risk)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 52 = printed p. 40) - every numeric cell dual-confirmed: the Table 18 grid confirmed THREE WAYS - the chapter djvu read (Ceiling 48%/32%, Wall 32%/12%, Ledge/bridge 5%/12%, Support Column 80%/4%), the compiled-tables appendix reprint (djvu.txt line 15559, the garble 4896 = 48%) and the Capture layer (the Support Column 80%/4% row and the example sequence) all agree; the djvu garble 648 = 6d8 settled by the Capture 6d8 read; the djvu garble 114damage = 1/4 damage settled by the Capture 1/4 read; the djvu 112 and 114 halves/quarters read as 1/2 and 1/4. The example side roll 33 exceeds the 32% wall chance, so exactly one side continues. The Defensive Point Values section starts the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: Table 18 pins as a 4x3 grid: the row key, the area-above percent and the area-next-to percent, each a d100 chance that collapses on an equal-or-less roll. The cascade divisors pin as exact integers (tertiary 2, subsequent 2, example secondary 2 and tertiary 4). The 4d8 damage pins as dice + sides consts per the R508 dsgbatt.h convention, with the 30-foot 12d8 example and its save-reduced 6d8. The R511 dsgcavein.h pins are the causes seam and nothing auto-credits.

audit_comment: The DSG chain reaction pins the opener (gravity constantly working destruction on underworld ceilings, a small cave-in weakening supporting structures for an immediate or near-future massive chain reaction, the nearby ceilings and walls checked, the per-section d100 vs Table 18 determining the extent), the chain reading (equal-or-less collapses the adjacent area at about the same area as the original, the miss within 10% of the chance significantly weakening the area that might collapse at any moment, the chain collapses forcing checks in all their adjacent areas, the tertiary chance half rounded up, each subsequent roll at 1/2 the forcing roll chance), the decayed exception (the DM may keep the original chance for all subsequent rolls in heavily eroded or ancient-ruin areas), the worked example (the 9th-level druid, the 100x80x10 ft transmuted ceiling, the 31-vs-48 collapse above, the 42-vs-24 hold of the second layer, the side rolls 12/65/97/33 with exactly one side continuing, the secondary checks at 1/2 and the tertiary at 1/4), the base area (the falling distance and rough landing on top, the bridge along its entire unsupported length, the tunnel ceiling never wider than the tunnel, the random 20x20 roughly square base area, the chain checks per adjacent square and above, radically increasing the total size), the falling layer (the three-foot assumption unless otherwise, the two-foot ceiling-and-floor example, the stone above a collapsed layer checked for a chain reaction), the falling damage (4d8 per 10 feet or less of thickness, the save vs petrification for half, the 30-foot 12d8 example reduced to 6d8), and the mud and water damage (mud, silt and sludgy substances at half rock damage with the save halving again, water at half with a save for 1/4, the damage for the first 10-foot thickness only, no additional damage from the weight of the pouring column, and the drowning risk).

consts.name: dnxWeakenedWithinPct
consts.comment: if the die roll does not indicate a collapse but is within 10% of the chance listed, the area is significantly weakened and might collapse at any moment.

consts.name: dnxTertiaryChanceDiv
consts.comment: the percentage chance for a tertiary collapse is half the chance for the original chain reaction cave-in.

consts.name: dnxSubsequentRollDiv
consts.comment: the divisor applied to the forcing roll chance for each subsequent chain reaction roll.

consts.name: dnxExampleDruidLevel
consts.comment: the example caster is a 9th-level druid using transmute rock to mud on a stone ceiling.

consts.name: dnxExampleSpellLengthFt
consts.comment: the spell affects an area of rock 100 feet long.

consts.name: dnxExampleSpellWidthFt
consts.comment: the spell area is 80 feet wide.

consts.name: dnxExampleSpellThickFt
consts.comment: the spell area is 10 feet thick, and all the stone in it converts to mud and falls.

consts.name: dnxExampleAboveRoll
consts.comment: the d100 roll for the area immediately above the mud ceiling is a 31, indicating another layer of rock falls on top of the mud.

consts.name: dnxExampleAboveSecondChance
consts.comment: the triggered roll for the rock on top of the stone that just fell is made at 1/2 the original probability, or 24.

consts.name: dnxExampleAboveSecondRoll
consts.comment: the next roll is a 42, greater than the 24 needed, so the second layer above does not collapse.

consts.name: dnxExampleSideRoll1
consts.comment: the first of the four d100 rolls checking the sides of the spell area for a chain reaction.

consts.name: dnxExampleSideRoll2
consts.comment: the second side roll.

consts.name: dnxExampleSideRoll3
consts.comment: the third side roll.

consts.name: dnxExampleSideRoll4
consts.comment: the fourth side roll.

consts.name: dnxExampleSecondaryDiv
consts.comment: the secondary checks have only 1/2 the chance listed on the chain reaction table, since the cave-in triggering them was itself a chain reaction.

consts.name: dnxExampleTertiaryDiv
consts.comment: a collapse triggered by a secondary check causes tertiary checks with only 1/4 the chance listed.

consts.name: dnxBaseAreaFtX
consts.comment: where the size of the cave-in must be determined randomly, such as the ceiling of a vast chamber, assume the base cave-in occurs in an area of 20 feet by 20 feet.

consts.name: dnxBaseAreaFtY
consts.comment: the other side of the assumed base area: 20 feet.

consts.name: dnxLayerThickFtDefault
consts.comment: if a layer of rock falls from a ceiling or wall, assume that the layer is three feet thick unless other considerations apply.

consts.name: dnxFloorLayerExampleFt
consts.comment: the example thin layer: two feet of stone.

consts.name: dnxFallingDamageDice
consts.comment: characters beneath an area of rock that collapses take an average base damage of 4d8 per character per 10 feet (or less) of thickness of fallen rock.

consts.name: dnxFallingDamageSides
consts.comment: the falling rock damage die: d8.

consts.name: dnxDamagePerThicknessFt
consts.comment: the damage reckoning unit: 10 feet of thickness, or less, per 4d8 of damage.

consts.name: dnxExampleThicknessFt
consts.comment: the worked example: a 30-foot thickness of rock crashing down on characters in a cavern.

consts.name: dnxExampleDamageDice
consts.comment: the 30-foot example thickness inflicts 12d8 points of damage on each character.

consts.name: dnxExampleSaveDice
consts.comment: the example saving throw vs. petrification reduces the 12d8 to 6d8 (the djvu garble 648, settled by the Acrobat layer read of 6d8).

consts.name: dnxMudDamageDiv
consts.comment: the mud/silt divisor: half of falling rock damage.

consts.name: dnxWaterDamageDiv
consts.comment: the falling water divisor: half of normal damage.

consts.name: dnxWaterSaveDiv
consts.comment: falling water allows a save for 1/4 damage (the djvu garble 114damage = 1/4, settled by the Acrobat layer).

consts.name: dnxWaterChargedThicknessFt
consts.comment: in the case of water the damage is inflicted for the first 10-foot thickness of falling material only.

consts.name: dnxT18RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 18 carries four original-location rows: ceiling, wall, ledge or bridge, and support column.

bools.name: dnxSmallCaveInWeakensSupports
bools.comment: the force of gravity is constantly working destruction on underworld ceilings; even a small cave-in can so weaken supporting structures that a massive chain reaction of collapse begins immediately or threatens an area in the near future.

bools.name: dnxAdjacentAreasMustBeChecked
bools.comment: when a cave-in occurs, the areas of nearby ceilings and walls must be checked to see if they weaken or collapse as a result of the original cave-in.

bools.name: dnxDmRollsD100PerSection
bools.comment: the DM rolls d100 and compares the result to Table 18: Cave-in Chain Reaction, rolling for each section of adjacent material, to determine the extent of the cave-in.

bools.name: dnxEqualOrLessCollapses
bools.comment: a d100 result that is equal to or less than the number listed indicates that the adjacent area has also collapsed.

bools.name: dnxCollapseSameAreaAsOriginal
bools.comment: the area of a chain reaction collapse is about the same as that of the original cave-in.

bools.name: dnxWeakenedMayCollapseAnyMoment
bools.comment: a significantly weakened area, missed by the chain reaction roll by less than the weakened band, might collapse at any moment.

bools.name: dnxChainCollapseForcesMoreChecks
bools.comment: areas that collapse as a result of a chain reaction force checks for chain reaction collapses in all adjacent areas.

bools.name: dnxTertiaryRoundedUp
bools.comment: the halved tertiary chance is rounded up.

bools.name: dnxEachSubsequentRollHalved
bools.comment: if the chain reaction continues, each subsequent roll is made with 1/2 the chance of the chain reaction roll that forced it.

bools.name: dnxDecayedIgnoresDecline
bools.comment: if an area is exceptionally weak and decayed, the DM may ignore the declining chance of a chain reaction cave-in and use the original cave-in chance for all subsequent rolls.

bools.name: dnxDecayedErodedOrAncient
bools.comment: the decayed exception is common in areas heavily eroded by water or other natural forces, or constructed long ago and left to fall into ruin.

bools.name: dnxExampleAboveCollapses
bools.comment: the example roll of 31 against the 48% ceiling chain reaction chance means the area above also collapses.

bools.name: dnxExampleSecondLayerHolds
bools.comment: the example second layer above the original collapse does not collapse.

bools.name: dnxExampleOneSideContinues
bools.comment: only one of the four sides of the spell area continues to collapse.

bools.name: dnxExampleSecondaryChecksRequired
bools.comment: the secondary collapse forces additional checks for the area immediately above it and for the areas to the three sides that have not already collapsed.

bools.name: dnxEffectDependsOnPositionAndRock
bools.comment: the effect of a cave-in upon characters and creatures in the area depends on where they are and the amount of rock that is falling.

bools.name: dnxOnTopUseFallingRules
bools.comment: if characters are on top of something that collapses, consider the distance fallen and treat the landing surface as rough, per the expanded falling rules (page 19).

bools.name: dnxBaseAreaFromStructure
bools.comment: the base area of a cave-in can often be determined by the structure or surface that is collapsing.

bools.name: dnxBridgeFallsUnsupportedLength
bools.comment: a bridge that collapses will collapse along its entire unsupported length.

bools.name: dnxTunnelCeilingNeverWider
bools.comment: a tunnel ceiling collapse can never be wider than the tunnel itself.

bools.name: dnxBaseAreaRoughlySquare
bools.comment: the randomly determined base cave-in area is roughly square in shape.

bools.name: dnxChainCheckedPerAdjacentSquare
bools.comment: chain reactions must be checked for each adjacent square area, as well as in the ceiling directly above the rock that has caved in.

bools.name: dnxChainRadicallyIncreasesSize
bools.comment: chain reactions radically increase the total size of a cave-in.

bools.name: dnxLayerThickUnlessOtherwise
bools.comment: the three-foot layer assumption yields to other considerations when they apply.

bools.name: dnxThinFloorLayerExample
bools.comment: a two-foot-thick layer of stone serving as a ceiling in one chamber and a floor in the one above is never more than two feet thick when it collapses.

bools.name: dnxThreeFtLeavesStoneCheckChain
bools.comment: if a three-foot-thick section of collapsing rock leaves additional stone above it, that stone should be checked for a chain reaction cave-in.

bools.name: dnxSavePetrificationHalf
bools.comment: characters beneath a collapse are allowed a saving throw vs. petrification for half damage.

bools.name: dnxMudHalfRockDamage
bools.comment: if the falling material is mud, silt, or any other sludgy substance, the damage inflicted on characters below is only half that caused by falling rock.

bools.name: dnxMudSaveHalvesAgain
bools.comment: characters beneath falling mud or silt are also entitled to a saving throw vs. petrification, which if successful halves this damage again.

bools.name: dnxWaterHalfRockDamage
bools.comment: falling water inflicts 1/2 of the normal damage.

bools.name: dnxWaterNoWeightDamage
bools.comment: even if the character remains under a column of pouring water, he does not sustain additional damage from the weight of the water.

bools.name: dnxWaterColumnDrowningRisk
bools.comment: a character under a column of pouring water is quite possibly unable to breathe and needs to escape the water or drown.

col_comments: the row key: 0 a ceiling, 1 a wall, 2 a ledge or bridge, 3 a support column.
the percent chance that the area above the original cave-in also collapses on a d100 roll equal to or less than this number.
the percent chance that the area next to the original cave-in also collapses on a d100 roll equal to or less than this number.
